title: Platform weeknotes: routing + auth + control plane (Feb 17–24, 2027)
body:
Purpose: quick noisy weeknotes to capture what the routing/auth/controlplane folks discussed while we're iterating on quota fallbacks and the new auth token rotation flow. Not polished — intentionally a snapshot for follow-ups.

Attendees (ad-hoc across syncs): Maya P, Diego M, Priya N, Liam O, Sara K, oncall: Toby R (shift A).

1) High-level status
- Running two parallel experiments: allocator-based throttling (experiment A) and dynamic fallback routing by model-capability (experiment B).
- Auth team pushed a beta of token rotation microservice (rotato) to staging; needs canary in us-west1 next week.
- Quota controller is still intermittently double-counting prefix cache hits when requests are retried. Root cause suspected in count-on-retry logic.

2) Telemetry snapshot (last 7 days) — rough numbers grabbed from quick query
- Avg controlplane request p95: 210ms (down from 235ms two weeks ago)
- Routing decision latency p50: 18ms, p95: 78ms (spikes when policy DB reloads)
- Auth token verification rate: 120k/s overall, peak 145k/s on Feb 22 10:15 UTC
- Error budget burn (controlplane): 2.3% — approaching the 2.5% threshold; need mitigation plan if trending up.

3) Experiment A: allocator-based throttling (Diego)
- Goal: reduce tail latency and decrease wasted GPU cycles by pre-emptively rejecting low-priority requests into a soft-queue.
- Implementation detail: new allocator field `soft_backpressure_factor` (0.6 default in staging) that rejects when queue/backlog ratio > threshold.
- Early result: 9% throughput drop for non-critical routes but 18% reduction in p99 generator latency for critical routes.
- Open issues: fairness across tenants (observed one mid-market customer at 40% lower success rate), need to add tenant-weighted fairness.
- Next steps: Diego to prototype tenant-weight weighting by 2027-02-28 (JIRA-PLT-1987).

4) Experiment B: fallback routing by model-capability (Priya)
- Goal: when primary model variant is overloaded, route to a cheaper quantized variant while preserving SDK contract.
- Approach: use capability manifests, choose fallback that matches `structured_output=true` etc.
- Problem: some downstream SDKs assume deterministic logits ordering; we added a shim but saw regressions in 2 customer tests.
- ETA for wider canary: 2027-03-03 after additional integration tests.

5) Auth token rotation (Sara)
- Rotato service status: staging -> canary plan drafted. Steps: rotate every 24h for service tokens, 7d for long-lived keys; support hot-reload of validation keyset.
- Planned canary: 2% traffic in us-west1 for 48h, then expand if no auth failures.
- Known risk: older SDKs that pin JWKS fetcher to 1h TTL — we will ship a compatibility shim.
- Action: Sara to add metrics for token acceptance failures + degradation signal by 2027-02-26.

6) Quotas and counting bug (Liam)
- Symptom: retries cause multiple billing counts for the same logical request when prefix cache hit occurs mid-retry.
- Short-term mitigation: disable count-on-retry for routes with KV-cache suffix until patch lands. This will be toggled via feature flag.
- Long-term fix: move to idempotency token check in quota service. Design doc in progress (linked: CONFLUENCE-PLTFM-723).
- Owner: Liam O'Connor, patch expected 2027-03-04.

7) Incident follow-up (Feb 22 spike)
- What happened: policy DB reload coincided with auth key rotation in staging -> transient routing fallback to regional model variants causing 1.5x cost for 6 min.
- Why: ordering of reloads not tolerant; race between policy update handler and keyset refresh.
- Action items: add mutex ordering + backoff, and test harness for concurrent controlplane state changes. Estimated PR by 2027-02-25 (owner: Maya).

8) Oncall notes / handoff (Toby)
- Observed higher than usual 429s for one enterprise customer around 03:00 PST; traced to tenant-weight config in allocator experiment — rolled back experiment for that tenant.
- Handoff: Toby -> next oncall (Nirali) notes to watch: errors with prefix-cache, and auth failure spike metric `auth.rotate.failures`.

9) Decisions / policy
- Keep experiment A running but reduce default `soft_backpressure_factor` from 0.6 -> 0.5 in prod canary to improve fairness.
- Approve canary for rotato (2%, 48h) once compatibility shim merged.

10) Action items (short list)
- Diego: tenant-weighted fairness prototype for allocator by 2027-02-28. (JIRA-PLT-1987)
- Priya: finish integration tests for capability-based fallback; aim for canary 2027-03-03.
- Sara: add token-rotation degradation metrics + alert (`SLO: auth-rotation-success-rate`) by 2027-02-26.
- Liam: implement idempotency token check for quota counting; PR by 2027-03-04.
- Maya: PR to enforce reload ordering + test harness by 2027-02-25.
- Oncall: keep experiment A feature flag ready to toggle per-tenant; update runbook with rollback steps. (owner: oncall rotation)

11) Open questions / parking lot
- Does tenant-weighting create a new vector for noisy-neighbor cost? need cost modelling. (Finance consult: reach out to Anya in FinOps)
- How should we expose fallback routing visibility in Console? product wants a lightweight signal per request. Priya to sync with Console PM.
- Should short-lived service tokens be rotated more frequently for high-throughput services? security to weigh CPU/cost tradeoff.

12) Quick scratchpad (notes to self)
- Remember to update /doc/allocator/tenant-weighting.md after Diego's prototype.
- Add a small dashboard tile for `quota.double_count_rate` and pin to Platform Ops board.
- Draft language for customer email if experiment A toggles per-tenant: include explicit mention of temporary throttling and how to opt-out.

Appendix: small capacity table (rough) — estimate of effective capacity impact in staging with experiment A on:

RouteType | baseline qps | with-expA qps | p99 latency change
critical  | 1200        | 1160         | -18%
standard  | 3400        | 3100         | +4%
batch     | 600         | 480          | +12%

(rough numbers; will be fleshed out in a follow-up sheet).

If anything is missing or you want more detail on an item, add a comment here or ping in slack:#platform-routing.

— Maya
